sections.title: Section 1: Relationship with the Design Engineer(s)

questions.text: Have we previously worked with this engineer?
Are the design documents (plans and specifications) complete?
Is the design free of readily apparent problems?
Is there a reasonable procedure for the administration of change orders?
Is there a reasonable procedure for the administration of punch-list items?
Is there a reasonable process for the administration/approval of shop drawings and submittals?

sections.title: Section 2: Relationship with the Owner/Construction Manager/General Contractor (from prior experience or by reputation)

questions.text: Does the GC/CM treat bid in an ethical manner during the bidding process?
Does the GC/CM have a good reputation for their working relationship with electrical contractors
Does the GM/CM have a reputation or history of making progress payments on time?
Is additional work expected to be performed?
Does the GC/CM coordinate between trades effectively in the project?
Does the GC/CM have a realistic expectation of the scheduled time for the completion of the project?
Does the language of the Bid Form require the assumption of major risk (such as change order clauses, no damage for delay, and/or different site conditions)?
Is the language of the bid clear about what is included/excluded in the scope of work?
Is the time allowed for bid preparation proportional to the complexity and size of the project?
Are there enough estimating personnel available to complete bid preparation in the allocated time?
Does the bidding process create risk/opportunity (new market, new client, etc)?
Is the number of bidders on the bidders list an advantage or disadvantage? [Advantage equals a positive rating, disadvantage equals a minus rating]
Have we been successful in prior bidding encounters with the contractors on the bidders list?
Do we feel that after assessing the competition, we have a reasonable chance of being awarded the contract?
Is this a bidding opportunity (a new market, a new partnership, a new area, etc)?
Are we familiar with this type of project?
Are we comfortable with this size of project?
Has this type of work been reasonably profitable in the past?
Do we have past cost data available from similar projects?
Is this ‘our kind’ of project?
Do unique construction methods create a risk/opportunity?
Does the project require hazardous work (e.g. asbestos, contaminated soils, etc.)? Is this a risk or an opportunity?
Does the completion date allow for a realistic schedule?
If the project requires complex phasing, is this a risk or an opportunity?
Does the project expose us to unusual safety risks?
Is the project of adequate size for us to be competitive?
Has the client set a realistic budget?
Do we need the project for our field personnel and/or management?
Is this an area we are familiar with, and do we have relationships with all parties involved (i.e. city/state officials, business managers, and union leaders)?
Does the location create risk or opportunity?
Does the project location create risk in terms of distance/housing availability/housing quality?
Are unusual transportation problems caused by the site location?
Does the labor market at the site create risk or opportunity?
Are there restrictive union practices (such as mobility language or prefabrication) on the number of our own personnel we can use?
Are there other large projects competing for labor in the area?
Are there any unusual or nonstandard IBEW agreements or practices in place in the project area?
Do anticipated/typical weather conditions during the project’s scheduled timeframe create risk or opportunity?
Are we currently licensed to conduct business in the project area?
Do we have adequate project management personnel available to staff the project if we are awarded the contract?
Do we have the type of equipment necessary for the project, and is it available during the project timeframe?
Is there a Project Labor Agreement (PLA) in place for this project?
Are project management/filed supervisors available to be involved in the bidding process?
Is the contract reasonable and fair to all concerned?
Will further contracts/amendments follow?
Is the specified length of warranty for the project reasonable?
Is the basis for payment acceptable?
Is the rate of retainage nonstandard or otherwise unusual?
Do liquidated damages/incentives create risk or opportunity?
Are there insurance/indemnification requirements that create risk?
Is the work around an operating unit?
Is there adequate space to store, stage, and install materials on site?
Is overtime required?
Is shiftwork required?
Is the owner supplying materials (incl. bread-and-butter items such as conduit and wire)?
Is the owner supplying major equipment?
Are there anticipated access constraints to the site or project area?
